results.title: University hostels and rent control: Examining the Law and its limitations
results.content: Back in 1963, when Ghana passed its Rent Act, university accommodation was nothing like the commercial hostels we have today. It was mostly halls of residence, institutional, part of the educational experience. Sixty years on, that has changed. Hostels built for purpose, decent fees, private capital and company management systems have turned student hostels into big business. But the legislation that regulates residential tenancies has not changed. And so, the question of whether university hostels are covered by the Rent Act has come up recently. If you pay for a hostel, are you a tenant? Does the Rent Control Department have the same regulatory powers as it does over other tenancies? And, most importantly, can we use 60-year-old legislation to regulate something its drafters could not have imagined? results.title: Nitiwul accuses government of buying two VIP aircraft for President in one year
results.content: Former Defence Minister Dominic Nitiwul has accused the government of acquiring two VIP aircraft for the President within a year, questioning the purchase of an Airbus H175 helicopter alongside the Falcon 6X executive jet. Contributing to the debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 19, 2026, Mr Nitiwul argued that the Airbus H175 was designed for civilian rather than military purposes. Referring to paragraphs in the Budget Statement, he said the helicopter should be considered alongside the Falcon 6X when assessing the government's aircraft acquisitions. “On page 158, paragraph 475, this aircraft that you went and bought, Airbus H175, it's meant for civilian purposes. It's not a military aircraft. Same thing as 168. It's a civilian-branded aircraft. So you bought two VIP aircraft for the President. Two. In one year,” he stated.

results.title: Nitiwul questions purchase of new presidential jet, says Falcon 900EX is serviceable
results.content: Former Defence Minister Dominic Nitiwul has questioned the government’s decision to acquire a new presidential aircraft, insisting that the existing Falcon 900EX remains serviceable and in good condition. The government has confirmed the acquisition of a new Falcon 6X executive jet for the Ghana Air Force. Parliament approved the purchase on December 4, 2025. Contributing to the debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 19, 2026, he said the aircraft had undergone extensive servicing under both the previous and current administrations. “The current jet, Falcon 900 EX, is serviceable. That means that it's working. It is working because we, led by myself, took it to the South of France and serviced it for 12 months. Your government further serviced it for another six months,” he stated.

results.title: Amin Adam accuses government of failing to account for jobs promised in previous budgets
results.content: Ranking member on Parliament's Finance Committee, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has accused the government of failing to account for jobs promised under previous budgets, arguing that the 2027 Budget does not adequately address the employment and cost-of-living challenges facing Ghanaians. Contributing to the debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 19, 2026, the Karaga MP said Ghanaians had expected the budget to provide answers to their immediate concerns, particularly joblessness and the rising cost of living. "Unfortunately, Mr Speaker, this budget failed the test. The budget failed the test because it could not account for jobs promised in the 2025 budget and in the 2026 budget," he stated.
